mission_1.search: BFS and A* both found the same path length of 13.5. However, BFS expanded 928 nodes, while A* expanded 700 nodes, so A* examined fewer cells. In my BFS code, I used frontier.popleft() to explore cells in the order they were added to the queue. In A* I used  heappush() and heappop()  to select the cell with the lowest priority, calculated using g + ctx.heuristic(nxt). This allows A* to focus more on cells closer to the goal instead of exploring level by level like BFS.
mission_1.failure: On the constrained map BFS had a path length of 24.5, while DFS had a path length of 50.0. This means BFS found a shorter path than DFS. This is because BFS explores cells level by level using a queue, while DFS explores one direction deeper before going back and checking other directions. IDDFS had a path length of 0.0 because its status was resource_limit meaning it used up its allowed resources before it could finish searching and find a path. For the unreachable case no_path means the algorithm finished searching but could not find a path from the start to the goal. On the other hand, resource_limit means the algorithm used up its allowed time or expansions before it could finish searching. I used AI to help me understand and implement the four search algorithms. I also ran the small tests to check my code and looked at the results to understand how the algorithms work and how they differ.
